latin_text: neque enim plantam cortex, sed stupida et nihil sentiens natura; neque iumenta corium, sed bruta anima et sensualis; nec caelum orbiculatum corpus, sed recta ratio; nec sequestratio corporis, sed spiritalis intelligentia angelum facit.
english_translation: It is not in fact the bark that makes the plant, but dull and insentient nature; not the hide that makes a beast of burden, but a brutish and sensuous soul; not the circular body that makes the heavens, but straightforward reason; not the separation from the body that makes an angel, but its spiritual intelligence.
exegesis: Pico defines angelhood ontologically through form (intelligentia spiritualis), not matter. This negates metempsychotic transmigration and grounds angelic transformation in moral and intellectual actualization—a doctrine compatible with Christian anthropology.
notes: Pico defines angelhood ontologically: not a physical form, but spiritual intelligence (intellectus). This refutes metempsychosis and establishes that becoming an angel is a moral and intellectual transformation.
